answer.rationale: Both observed declines (onboarding completion -4%, activation -6%) are plausibly linked, with completion upstream of activation, so a single onboarding-shortening test can move both metrics rather than treating the symptom. memory_86 and memory_31 both point this direction, which is why memory_86 is worth verifying: the inherited summaries are qualitative ('improved completion rates', 'durable lift') with no effect sizes, no measurement window, and no segment definition, so I cannot tell whether the prior lift was large enough to offset a 4-6% QoQ decline or whether it was a self-serve-only effect. I want the original record before committing the only slot this week. I am verifying memory_73 because promotional_pricing is the direction the competitor's entry pricing most tempts, and memory_73 is the memory best dressed up to justify it: it is the only entry with crisp numbers (+31% signup, +18% rev), which makes it feel more verified than the others when in fact it reports only a 12-week reporting window, no retention or margin figures, and no qualified-revenue definition. A signup lift under discounting is exactly the pattern that can be adverse selection, pulling in price-sensitive accounts that churn after the discount lapses; against a primary objective of sustainable long-term qualified revenue that record does not yet support action, and matching a competitor on price also risks a durable reset of willingness-to-pay across the SMB book. I am not verifying memory_57 or memory_44 because referral incentives address neither declining metric and enterprise sales-assist targets a segment that is not where the pressure is. Downstream value risk is flagged on two counts: the discount path above, and the onboarding action itself, since cutting required fields removes qualification and routing signal, so I will hold lead-quality and 90-day retention as guardrail metrics rather than reading activation alone. Standard experiment scale with a holdout, not a broad rollout, because the supporting memories are directionally consistent but quantitatively thin, and the current declines may have a cause (competitor-driven mix shift in who is signing up) that no inherited memory covers. If the memory_86 archive shows the prior lift was small, narrow, or measured only on a short window, I would shift the slot to activation_messaging as the more directly targeted intervention.
